findings.F1: Across all bars, whatever the trend, the range ratio (the day's high-low range over its 30-day mean) separates the next 5 days clearly: the upper half's mean excess 5-day return is +0.89 % and the lower half's is −0.89 %, a difference of 0.0178 with Welch t 5.22 on 6046 non-overlapping cases; the sign is positive in 19 of 19 coins and in 6 of 8 years (Spearman 0.091).
findings.F2: The effect is as large in falling coins (20-day return ≤ 0), which the tested idea leaves out. There the upper half earns +0.38 % against −1.06 % for the lower half, a difference of 0.0144 with Welch t 3.24 on 3074 cases, positive in 19 of 19 coins and 6 of 8 years. It is graded by quintile (−0.72 %, −1.32 %, −1.26 %, +0.44 %, +1.15 %, top quintile t 2.66), and it matches the uptrend difference (0.0149, t 2.89, 17 of 19 coins).
findings.F3: In falling coins the day's direction does not matter. Wide-range down days and wide-range up days end the next 5 days alike (+0.41 % vs +0.38 %, difference 0.0003, t 0.05). The down-day top range quintile earns +1.44 % (t 2.45, mean ratio 2.09), and the up-day top two quintiles earn +0.83 % and +0.60 % (t about 1.0).
findings.F4: The falling-coin effect is uneven over time. Its yearly Spearman is 0.29 in 2024, 0.17 in 2025, 0.14 in 2021 and 0.08 in 2022, but −0.03 in 2018 and −0.01 in 2023, so it rests mostly on recent years.
findings.F5: In rising coins, wide-range up days look better than wide-range down days (+1.56 % vs +0.50 % excess over 5 days), but the difference does not stand out from chance (Welch t 1.33, 831 vs 655 cases).
findings.F6: Nearness to the 30-day high has a pooled difference of 0.0139 with t 4.06, but it is positive in only 63 % of coins and 50 % of years. Recent volatility against its 60-day level shows nothing (difference 0.0026, t 0.70). Neither counts after this many angles.
findings.F7: The tested idea's size covers its cost. Its total move is +1.16 % per case over 5 days, 5.2 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade, and its unusual move is +0.35 % (strength 0.027), 1.6 times the cost. The book's Sharpe is 1.06 and its Calmar 0.94.

ideas.idea: The wider a coin's daily high-low range is relative to its average range over the past 30 days, the higher that coin's return over the next 5 days, while the coin's own 20-day return is negative.
ideas.consequence: A trader should read a sharply widened daily range in a falling coin as a reason to buy for the next 5 days, rather than as a sign that the fall will continue.
ideas.name: range expansion in downtrends
